To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The life cycle energy consumption and emissions of city centre apartments are higher than suburban dwellings, mainly due to higher car ownership and use, but lower than those in the inner suburbs, mainly due to lower energy consumption of apartments.

the total delivered energy consumption and emissions of apartment households were lower than that of suburban households, however the emissions per capita were higher than both inner and outer suburban dwellings.

The total life cycle energy use of households living in apartment buildings in Adelaide's CBD is lower than those living in conventional suburban housing due mainly to the higher car usage in the suburbs, however, the total greenhouse gas emissions of apartment dwellers are higher than those in the inner suburbs and comparable to those in the outer suburbs when calculated on a per capita and household basis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we might better design and plan our cities and suburbs to achieve a more sustainable built environment.
understanding the energy consumption of households and their transport behaviour.
the life-cycle energy consumption and emissions of city centre apartments compared with suburban dwellings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, on a per capita and per household basis, the total life cycle energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions of city centre apartments are higher than suburban dwellings.
the environmental performance of apartments in the inner city is not necessarily superior to that of suburban dwellings.

the environmental benefits of urban consolidation and higher density living are not automatic, and that they depend on a range of factors including the location of dwellings, the design of buildings, and the energy efficiency of buildings and their operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, while the environmental impact of apartment living in city centres can be lower than that of suburban living, the benefits are highly dependent on the energy efficiency of apartment buildings and the energy consumption of the households within them.
, for a sample of Adelaide households, there was little difference between the total energy and emissions from apartment dwellers compared to suburban dwellers.
, while the environmental impact of apartment living is less than that of conventional housing, it cannot be taken for granted that it is always lower.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environmental impacts of urban form are complex and that a simple comparison of urban density with low density is insufficient.
the environmental impacts of urban form and transport cannot be assessed without considering both the housing and transport components.
, while urban density may be a good thing for cities, it does not automatically lead to a lower per capita emissions outcome for residents.
